- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion or downward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; adjust upward to capture early rally momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 3–5% relative to prior 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows volatility >10% over 10-day window, reduce forecast slope to avoid overconfidence in linear trends.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and model shows steady upward trend, check for lag: true outcome often dips 1–3 days later; delay forecast by 1–2 days or add 1–2% downward correction.
